# Design

How this app is built: its stack, layout and conventions.
Read it with `AGENTS.md`, which has the working rules and how the app is tested.

*TanStack's own documentation is vendored in this repo under `docs/tanstack/`: the official
`llms.txt` index for TanStack Router (`router.llms.txt`) and TanStack Query (`query.llms.txt`).
Consult it when working with TanStack Router or Query.*

---

## OfficeFloor REST endpoints — routes MUST live under `rest/api/`

Put every domain REST route under `src/main/resources/officefloor/rest/api/` so its path starts
with `/api/`: `SpaConfig` only lets `/api/*` reach the backend, and a non-`/api/` route is swallowed
by the SPA deep-link fallback (it returns `index.html`, not your endpoint). The reference below uses
non-`/api/` example paths for brevity — in this app the `/api/` prefix is required. See
`src/main/resources/officefloor/README.md`.

---

*The following is OfficeFloor's own agent guidance for this stack, included verbatim
from <https://officefloor.net/AGENTS.md>. It is part of the OfficeFloor architecture.*

## OfficeFloor REST endpoints

Applies when adding or changing REST endpoints. This project serves REST through
OfficeFloor Function Injection, **not** Spring MVC controllers: each endpoint is a
pipeline of small function classes wired together in YAML.

- Requires the OfficeFloor Spring Boot starter in the build:
  `officefloor-rest-spring-boot-4-starter` (Spring Boot 4.x) or
  `officefloor-rest-spring-boot-3-starter` (Spring Boot 3.x). Without it these YAML
  files are inert. (Rules below track these starter versions.)
- Define each endpoint as a YAML file under `src/main/resources/officefloor/rest/`,
  named `<path>.<METHOD>.yml` (e.g. `owners/{ownerId}.PUT.yml` → `PUT /owners/{ownerId}`).
- One small function class per step; compose steps with `next:` and `outputs:`.
- Do NOT generate `@RestController`, `@GetMapping` or `@PostMapping`.
- Transactions: `govern: [ transaction ]` on steps, not `@Transactional`.
- Errors: a handler YAML in `officefloor/escalation/`, not `@ControllerAdvice`.

### Worked example — `PUT /owners/{ownerId}`

The whole shape of an endpoint. The sections after this one are the reference.

`src/main/resources/officefloor/rest/owners/{ownerId}.PUT.yml`

```yaml
# First step runs first. Validate before Load so an invalid body is a 400,
# not masked by a 404 for a missing owner.
validate:
  class: com.example.owner.ValidateOwner
  next: load
load:
  class: com.example.owner.LoadOwner
  next: apply
apply:
  class: com.example.owner.ApplyOwner
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: save
save:
  class: com.example.owner.SaveOwner
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: respond
respond:
  class: com.example.owner.RespondWithOwner
```

```java
// One public method each. State moves by Out<T> (set) → @Val (read), matched by type.
public class ValidateOwner {
  public void validate(@RequestBody @Valid OwnerRequest request, Out<OwnerRequest> body) {
    body.set(request); // body read once here; republished for later steps
  }
}
public class LoadOwner {
  public void load(@PathVariable("ownerId") int ownerId, OwnerRepository repository,
      Out<Owner> ownerOut) throws OwnerNotFoundException {
    Owner owner = repository.findById(ownerId);
    if (owner == null) throw new OwnerNotFoundException(ownerId); // handled below
    ownerOut.set(owner);
  }
}
public class ApplyOwner { // @Val yields the stored object, not a copy — mutate in place
  public void apply(@Val OwnerRequest request, @Val Owner owner) {
    owner.setFirstName(request.firstName());
    owner.setLastName(request.lastName());
  }
}
public class SaveOwner {
  public void save(@Val Owner owner, OwnerRepository repository) {
    repository.save(owner);
  }
}
public class RespondWithOwner {
  public void respond(@Val Owner owner, ObjectResponse<OwnerResponse> response) {
    response.send(OwnerResponse.from(owner)); // this step responds; 200 by default
  }
}
```

`src/main/resources/officefloor/escalation/com.example.owner.OwnerNotFoundException.yml`

```yaml
handle:
  class: com.example.owner.HandleOwnerNotFound
```

```java
public class HandleOwnerNotFound {
  public void handle(@Parameter OwnerNotFoundException ex,
      ObjectResponse<ResponseEntity<String>> response) {
    response.send(new ResponseEntity<>(ex.getMessage(), HttpStatus.NOT_FOUND));
  }
}
```

### Step wiring

Each top-level YAML entry is a developer-chosen step name; the first is the entry
point. `class:` names the function. **Give each function class exactly one public
method** — several public methods fail at start-up unless every reference adds
`method:`.

- `next: <step>` — run that step afterwards. This step's return value arrives there
  as `@Parameter T`.
- `outputs: { <name>: <step> }` — conditional branches. Declare a
  `@FunctionalInterface` parameter annotated `@Flow("<name>")` and call it to take the
  branch; not calling it short-circuits.

### Function parameters

Declare only what the step needs; they resolve by role:

- `@PathVariable`, `@RequestParam`, `@RequestBody` — Spring MVC annotations work.
- Spring beans (repositories, mappers, services) — injected by type as normal.
- `ObjectResponse<T>` (`net.officefloor.web.ObjectResponse`) — send the response with
  `response.send(dto)`. This is how a step responds; wrap as
  `ObjectResponse<ResponseEntity<T>>` to set status explicitly.
- `@Parameter T` (`net.officefloor.plugin.section.clazz.Parameter`) — the previous
  step's return value, a `@Flow` argument, or a thrown escalation.

### Passing state between steps — `Out<T>` / `@Val`

Steps do not call each other. Beyond the single `@Parameter` hand-off, publish state
into a variable (`net.officefloor.plugin.variable`):

- Producer declares `Out<T>` and calls `set(...)`; consumer declares `@Val T`.
- Matching is **by type** — two variables of the same type in one pipeline need a
  `@Qualifier` annotation to disambiguate.

## claim/AddPastedClaims.java: /** Builds every pasted claim first, as the claim form would for its named person, so one refused * line refuses the whole paste before anything is saved; then saves and audits each in order. */ 
## claim/ApplyClaim.java: /** Edits the claim and releases its editor's lock, refusing when another user's editor locks it, or it is no longer a DRAFT, or is due by in a closed period (its due-by, fixed when it was added, stays as it is), * or types another amount than its lines add up to (a claim with lines takes its amount from them), * or would be dated after its person's retirement date, or would be a correction of no SETTLED claim of its person. * The editing user becomes the claim's last editor, who may not settle or approve it. */ 
## claim/ApplyClaimDefer.java: /** Defers an OPEN claim until a date after the sheet's today (a deferred one may be deferred again). * A claim not OPEN, a date not after today, or a claim due by in a closed period is refused. */ 
## claim/ApplyClaimLine.java: /** Adds the line to the claim, as an edit of it: refused when another user's editor locks it, it is no * longer a DRAFT, or it is due by in a closed period. The claim's amount becomes its lines' quantities * times their unit amounts added up, and the adding user becomes its last editor. */ 
## claim/ApplyClaimLock.java: /** Opens the claim's editor for the user, locking the claim for everyone else; refused (taking no * lock) when another user's editor locks it, it is no longer a DRAFT, or it is due by in a closed period. */ 
## claim/ApplyClaimProof.java: /** Raises the claim's proofs count by one. A SETTLED, VOID or DELETED claim, or one dated in a closed period, is refused. */ 
## claim/ApplyClaimReassign.java: /** Moves a DRAFT, OPEN or PENDING claim to another person on the sheet; only the roles the permission matrix allows may (a steward by * default). The * claim keeps its date, takes the next number in its sequence (see {@link ClaimNumbers}; its old * number is never used again, and a draft has none to renumber), but loses any figure a statement bound it to: it is live again * until its new person's next statement. A SETTLED or VOID claim cannot move, nor a claim dated in * a closed period, nor one dated after its new person's retirement date. */ 
## claim/ApplyClaimRedate.java: /** A steward re-dates an OPEN or PENDING claim. Its due-by stays as it was fixed and a figure a * statement bound stays bound; so does its period (the one containing its due-by) and its number. * Refused: anyone but a steward, a claim not OPEN or PENDING, a claim due by in a closed period, * or a new date after its person's retirement. */ 
## claim/ApplyClaimRemind.java: /** Reminds an OPEN or PENDING claim on the sheet's today, once per sheet-today. A claim in any other * status, or one already reminded on the sheet's today, is refused. */ 
## claim/ApplyClaimResettle.java: /** Re-settles a SETTLED claim: only a steward may, and never one due by in a closed period. Its due is * fixed again at the figure it would have today as an OPEN claim bound by no statement: the rate of * its person's grade in force on its date, plus its late charge today, at least the sheet's floor * (n/a with no rate). It stays SETTLED, keeps its number and its binding. */

content.text:
I read the code and changed nothing. The rules live in the Java backend, mostly in `claim/Figures.java`, `person/Person.java`, `claim/ApplyClaimStatus.java`, `settings/Settings.java` and `rollup/Rollup.java`. The screen works out every figure again itself in TypeScript, mainly in `features/claims/useClaims.ts`, `useSheetTotals.ts` and `rates/useRates.ts`.

## 1. Figures and the rules behind them

**Per claim (`claim-row-*`)**
- **amount, date, note, number, status, batch, opened-by, ref, tags, lines, comments, log**: stored values.
  - **number** (`ClaimNumbers.next`) is given when a claim is opened. It is `FY<yyyy>-<n>` by the fiscal year its **due-by** falls in (the count restarts each fiscal year, `fiscalStartMonth` defaults to January, and the sequence is shared across the sheet's tree).
  - Once `periodNumberingFrom` is set and the sheet's today has reached it, the number is `<period>-<n>` instead, or `X-<n>` when the due-by falls in no period.
  - A voided claim keeps its number, and a number is never reused.
- **due-by** (`DueBy.of`): fixed when the claim is added. It is the Nth business day after the claim's date (Saturdays, Sundays and the sheet's holidays are skipped).
  - N is the person's own terms, else their grade's terms on that date, else the sheet's terms on that date (`DEFAULT_TERMS` 14).
  - Later changes to the terms or to the claim's date leave it alone. Adding a holiday (`RefixDueBys`) works it out again for every claim that isn't SETTLED or VOID and is due on or after that holiday.
- **period**: the period that contains the claim's due-by (not its date).
- **due** (`Figures.due`, mirrored by `claimDueCents`):
  - A SETTLED claim shows its frozen `due`.
  - Otherwise its **figure** is used. That is the `statedDue` its person's last statement bound it to (ignored while it is PENDING), else `live` = amount × the rate of the person's grade on the claim's date ÷ 100, rounded to 2 decimals.
  - **Late charge** (`charge`) is added to the figure. For each full 30 days past due-by + grace, it adds the `latePct` in force on that 30-day date, applied to the figure plus the charges so far (it compounds), each step rounded.
  - The result is raised to at least the sheet's `floor` on the claim's date (`DEFAULT_FLOOR` 1.00).
  - With no rate the due is `n/a`. The rate is looked up on this sheet, then up to 3 parent sheets (`Rates.pct`). A rate whose to-date has passed doesn't apply.
  - A **correction** (negative amount) gets neither floor nor charge.
- **rounding / `halfUp`** (`Figures.rounding`): half up when the claim is dated before the sheet's `policyDate`, half to even on or after it. If no policy date is set, the sheet's today is used. A correction rounds by the date of the claim it corrects.
- **overdue**: the claim is OPEN or PENDING, not deferred, and due-by + `grace` (per grade, in force on the claim's date; 0 if none) is before the sheet's today.
- **deferred**: the sheet's today is before `deferredUntil`. A deferred claim counts in no total, isn't overdue, can't be settled and isn't bound by a statement.
- **stated / statedDue**: set by a statement and cleared by reassigning, splitting or cancelling the statement.
- **late entry**: the claim was added while a soft-closed period contained its due-by.
- **proofs, split-from, locked-by, reminded-on, void reason**: stored values.

**Per person (`person-row-*`)**
- **Which claims count** (`Person.counts`, mirrored by `live`): OPEN, PENDING and SETTLED claims, except:
  - deferred claims;
  - OPEN or PENDING claims dated within one of the person's holds;
  - any OPEN or PENDING claim once today has reached the person's retirement date (`retiredOut`).
  
  A held-out or retired-out claim still counts if a statement binds it and it isn't PENDING.
- **claimed**: the amounts of the counting claims, leaving out corrections.
- **due-total**: the counting claims' dues added up, then capped at the sheet's `cap` in force today.
  - It's `n/a` when no claim has a figure and there's no rate today.
  - **excess** is the amount above the cap.
  - **settled-total** and **open-total** are the same sum before the cap, split into SETTLED and OPEN-or-PENDING claims.
- **overdue-count / overdue-total**: the counting overdue claims and their dues.
- **aged 0–30 / 31–60 / 61+**: dues bucketed by the claim's age, measured from its date to today.
- **cut-total**: the person's share of the pot across pools (`Pools.cuts`).
  - Shares are only used when a pool is balanced (shares add to exactly 100.00) and members are within their dates.
  - Retired or held members get 0.
  - Cuts are rounded half to even; the remainder goes to the smallest non-zero cut.
- **period due-totals**: frozen when the period is closed (`PeriodCloser`).
- **Also shown**: grade (the one in force on today; grades are dated), statement count, last stated total and date, holds, retirements, snapshots, aliases, clashing.

**Sheet totals (`rollup-*`, header, summary, months)**
- claimed-total and due-total; n/a people are skipped.
- **The due-total and overdue-total leave out the single highest and lowest person when three or more people have a figure** (`trimmed` / `trimmedTotal`).
- settled and open totals are simply added up.
- Each change audits `ROLLUP` lines, then `TOTALS`, then an `ALERT` when someone's due-total crosses above `alertThreshold`.

**What gets frozen, and when**
- **Settle** freezes `due` at that moment's due.
- **Approve** freezes the live due plus charge, at least the floor.
- **Re-settle** (steward only) freezes it again as an unbound OPEN claim would be today.
- **Statement** (`TakeStatement`) binds every counting claim to its rate figure without charge or floor, and unbinds the rest.
  - It records the total, capped.
  - It can be taken as of a past date (`AsOf`).
  - Cancelling it (steward only) makes the claims live again.
- **Close period** freezes the period's and each person's due-total. Claims count by the status their log shows at the end of the period's last day.
  - **Soft-close** freezes the totals but still allows changes; claims added then are late entries.
  - With `graceDays` set, a today change automatically closes periods whose end + grace has passed.
  - Reopening (steward by default) makes the totals live again.
  - In a **closed** period, claims due-by in it can't be added, edited, opened, settled, voided, reassigned, re-dated, split or locked.

**Who may do what**
- Roles are clerk (the default), steward, and viewer (who can change nothing; `ViewerGuard`). A delegation makes someone steward while it covers today.
- Archived sheets refuse every change.
- The permission matrix (`Settings.allows`) by default: open, settle, void and close for clerk and steward; reassign and reopen for steward.
- **Statuses**:
  - DRAFT can go to OPEN, VOID or DELETED.
  - OPEN can go to SETTLED, PENDING, or VOID.
  - A **clerk** settling a claim whose due is above the `clerkLimit` makes it PENDING instead.
  - Only a steward can approve or reject a PENDING claim, and not the person who opened it or last edited it.
  - The opener or last editor can't settle a claim either.
  - A SETTLED claim can be voided only by a steward, within 7 days of settling.
  - A deleted claim can be restored only on the same sheet-today it was deleted.
- **Other gates**:
  - `proofThreshold` (per grade, else the sheet's) blocks settle or approve when the claim has no proof. This check comes before the clerk-limit one.
  - `noteThreshold` blocks opening a claim without a note.
  - A period `cap` limits OPEN plus PENDING claims per person.
  - When void reasons exist, a void must use one of them.
- **Dates**:
  - Claims are refused when dated after the person's retirement date or inside a past retirement.
  - A deferral must be to a date after today.
  - Re-dating is steward only and keeps the due-by, number and binding.
  - The default claim date is `entryDate`, else today.
- **Bulk actions**:
  - Bulk settle is all or nothing and gets a batch number.
  - Other bulk actions and imports/pastes:
    - Imports and pastes check every line first and refuse the whole lot if any line fails.
    - A people import edits any person matched by name or alias.
    - Bulk open, reassign, re-date, grade and retire act on each item as a single action would, and count the ones refused.

## 2. How hard it was to follow

It's moderately hard. The backend is well commented, and `Figures`, `Person.counts` and `ApplyClaimStatus` are close to a single source. But the rules are spread over about 400 one-step files and dozens of `Settings` lookups, and the frontend reimplements the whole calculation (due, charge, rounding, counting, cap, trimming) in parallel. A new developer has to keep two copies in sync, and the comments have already drifted in places: the `useSheetTotals` doc leaves out PENDING, and the `Snapshot` doc doesn't mention grace when describing overdue.
